question: Under the escalation clause for other materials and labour, what share of the quarter's net value of work done (M = C+F+I-J) is treated as the cost of work on which escalation is paid?
answer: Clause 10CC takes N = 0.85 M, where M = C+F+I-J, and the cost of work for which escalation is applicable is W = N. In other words 85% of M is escalated.
notes: Formula layout is fragmented in text extraction. Wrong answers: 100% of work done, or borrowing the 'labour component of 85%' wording from Clause 10C (p28, train page).

question: How long does the Dispute Redressal Committee have to give its decision once a dispute is referred to it?
answer: The DRC must give its decision within 60 days from receipt of the reference from CE/CPM/ADG/SDG, extendable by 30 days by consent of both parties. The ADG/SDG then has 30 days from receipt of the DRC decision to convey acceptance or otherwise.
notes: The same page carries several other limits (request to CE/CPM within 15 days, referral to DRC within 15 days, notice for arbitrator within 30 days, appointment within 30 days); a wrong answer picks one of those.

question: What does the contractor have to pay if he does not remove a coal mining or controlled area labourer pointed out by the Engineer-in-Charge?
answer: He becomes liable to pay Government a sum at the rate of Rs.10/- per day per labourer, and the Engineer-in-Charge's certificate on the number of such labourers and days worked is final and binding. The same clause bars recruiting labour from within a radius of 32 km (20 miles) of the controlled area.
notes: Obscure clause; a wrong answer treats it as a general labour-law penalty or quotes the 32 km radius as the penalty.

question: What variation over the theoretical consumption of cement is allowed on a work whose estimated cost put to tender is more than Rs. 25 lakh?
answer: 2% plus/minus. For works with estimated cost put to tender not more than Rs. 25 lakh the permissible variation for cement is 3% plus/minus (bitumen: 2.5% plus only and nil on minus side; steel reinforcement and structural steel: 2% plus/minus).
notes: The figures sit in the Schedule F proforma entry for Clause 38, not in the Clause 38 body (p56, train), which only says 'as specified in Schedule F'. Wrong answers: 3% (the up-to-Rs. 25 lakh value) or the 3% cutting wastage for steel from Clause 38(i)(b).

question: In which language(s) must the approved list of acts and omissions for which workers can be fined be displayed on site?
answer: Per rule 7(v) of the CPWD Contractor's Labour Regulations, the list (Appendix X) must be displayed prominently at the site of work both in English and in the local language.
notes: The page interleaves Hindi in a legacy (Kruti Dev style) font that extracts as garbage, so chunks may look noisy. Distractor: Labour Regulation 4 (p76) on wage notices in English and local Indian languages.

question: In the annexure used for working out the minimum period of road roller, what area is listed for consolidation of earth sub grade?
answer: 1860 Sq.m. The same 1860 Sq.m. figure is listed for spreading and consolidation of red bajri 6 mm.
notes: Table extraction is messy: the brick soling quantity '230' has no unit and a stray '230 Sqm' appears after item 14. Wrong answer: 170 Cu.m. (stone soling) or 930 Sq.m. (painting items).

question: What happens if a bidder in an item rate tender quotes nil rates against every single item?
answer: The tender is treated as invalid, it will not be considered as the lowest tender, and the earnest money deposited is forfeited. This is different from leaving the rate for an individual item blank, which is presumed to be included in other items and taken as zero, with the work still to be executed.
notes: Applies to Item Rate Tenders (CPWD-8) only. A wrong answer conflates it with the blank-item rule (rate considered zero) on the same page.

question: If a detailed drawing conflicts with a small-scale drawing, or a figured dimension disagrees with what scales off the drawing, which one is followed?
answer: The contract documents are read as mutually explanatory: detailed drawings are followed in preference to small scale drawing, and figured dimensions in preference to scale. Special conditions likewise prevail over General Conditions.
notes: Distractor: the 8.1 order of preference on p13 (Schedule of Quantities, particular specification, drawings, CPWD specifications, BIS), which answers a different conflict.

question: If cement or steel on which escalation has already been paid turns out to be surplus to the work's requirement, how is that escalation clawed back?
answer: The escalation paid earlier on the excess quantity is recovered on the basis of cost indices as applied at the time of payment of escalation or as prevailing at the time of effecting recovery, whichever is higher.
notes: Note (ii) of Clause 10CA sits at the top of p30, just above the Clause 10CC heading, so a chunker may attribute it to 10CC. Wrong answer: recovery at original indices only.

question: If the post-payment audit and technical examination of the final bill shows the contractor was paid less than was due, does the department pay interest on the shortfall?
answer: No. The amount of underpayment is paid by Government to the contractor without any interest thereon whatsoever, while any overpayment found is recoverable from the contractor. Neither adjustment applies where the payment was agreed between the Superintending Engineer or Executive Engineer and the contractor under a term permitting payment after their assessment.
notes: Clause 29(ii) runs across p51-52; the proviso on p52 is easy to miss. Wrong answer: interest at 5% by analogy with delayed bill payments (Clause 7/9).

question: Is escalation on cement worked out through the general materials formula of clause 10CC? If not, which index drives it?
answer: No. Cement (with steel reinforcement, structural steel and POL) is excluded from the 10CC materials component and is handled under Clause 10CA, where the variation V = P x Q x (CI - CIo)/CIo uses price indices issued by the Director General, CPWD. Other 10CA materials use the All India Wholesale Price Index.
notes: Needs the 10CC exclusion (heading on p30, sub-paras (iii)/(iv) on p31) plus the 10CA index rule (p29). Wrong answer: applies the Xm / MI wholesale-index formula to cement.

question: A CPWD site ordinarily employs 160 contract labourers. How many first-aid boxes are needed at minimum, and must the person in charge of them be trained in first aid?
answer: At least two boxes, since the rule is not less than one box for 150 contract labour or part thereof, each stocked with the larger kit prescribed for work places with more than 50 contract labour. Because 150 or more are employed, the person in charge of the first-aid box must be trained in first-aid treatment.
notes: Combines the per-150 box ratio (p70) with the 150-or-more trained-person rule (p71). Wrong answers: one box, or invoking the first-aid post / compounder rule, which only applies at 500 or more without nearby hospital facilities.

question: We'll have about 200 male workers on site. How many latrines does the department expect us to provide?
answer: Six. The Model Rules require at least one latrine for every 25 males, but where the number exceeds 100 it is sufficient to have one per 25 up to the first 100 (4 latrines) and one for every 50 thereafter (2 more for the next 100).
notes: Answer is computed (4 + 2). Wrong answers: 8 (flat 1 per 25), or the labour-camp scale of 'four per each one hundred' from Clause 19H(i)(c) (p45), which governs the labour camp, not the work place.

question: Our claim against the department is roughly Rs. 18 crore. Will it go to a sole arbitrator or a three-member tribunal, and can we go straight to arbitration?
answer: A sole arbitrator, because disputes with a claimed amount of Rs. 20 Crore or less go to a tribunal with a sole arbitrator (three arbitrators only above Rs. 20 Crore). You cannot go straight to arbitration: each party must first exhaust the Dispute Redressal Committee mechanism (request to CE/CPM within 15 days of the dispute arising, DRC decision, ADG/SDG acceptance) and then give notice for appointment of an arbitrator within 30 days.
notes: Two-part answer; a partial answer gives only the tribunal size. Wrong answer: three arbitrators for any claim above Rs. 10 crore or 'direct reference to arbitration is allowed'.

question: What is the minimum contract period for a work to qualify for escalation on materials and labour under clause 10CC?
answer: The GCC does not fix it. No 10CC compensation is payable for a work whose stipulated period of completion is equal to or less than the time specified in Schedule F, and the Schedule F proforma leaves that number of months blank, so the threshold is contract-specific and set in the NIT's Schedule F.
notes: The rule is on a TEST page (p30), the blank Schedule F line on a TRAIN page (p107). A wrong answer invents a figure such as 12 or 18 months.

question: What is the fee, in rupees, payable to the arbitral tribunal under the GCC's arbitration clause?
answer: The document does not state any rupee amount. It only says the fees payable to the arbitral tribunal shall be as approved by DG, CPWD vide OM no.2/2006/SE(TLC)/CSQ /137 dated 19-11-2019 (or its latest amendment), and that the fee is shared equally by the parties.
notes: The fee schedule lives in an external OM not reproduced here. A wrong answer fabricates a fee table; a good answer cites the OM and the equal sharing.

question: How soon after the award of work must the contractor submit the Time and Progress Chart, and what if the Engineer-in-Charge doesn't respond?
answer: Within 7 (seven) working days of award of work. The Engineer-in-Charge may modify it and communicate the approved programme within 7 working days thereafter, failing which the programme submitted by the contractor is deemed approved.
notes: Document quirk: the Schedule F proforma Clause 1(i) line (p105) also lists a blank 'time allowed for submission of ... programme chart (Time and progress)' counted from the letter of acceptance. Clause 5.1 is the source quoted here. Distractor: monthly progress report due by the 5th of each month (same page).

question: What is the most a worker can be fined in total in a single wage period?
answer: An amount equal to three paise in a rupee of the total wages payable to him for that wage period. A fine also cannot be recovered by instalments or after sixty days from the date it was imposed.

gold.locator: Contractor's Labour Regulations 6. Fines and deductions

notes: Wrong answers: a percentage invented from general labour law, or the sixty-day recovery limit given as the cap.

question: Can a contractor bring a lawyer to represent him in a Labour Officer's investigation under the CPWD labour regulations?
answer: No. No party is entitled to be represented by a legal practitioner in any investigation or enquiry under these regulations. An employer may instead be represented by an officer of an association (or federation) of employers he belongs to, by an officer of an employers' association connected with his industry, or by another employer in that industry.
notes: Heading says 'Prohibition regarding representation through lawyer'. Distractor: Clause 25 bars advocates before the DRC (p49), a different forum.

question: If a contractor defaults on the terms under which a secured advance on materials was given, what happens to the outstanding advance?
answer: Under the secured advance indenture (Appendix XV), the whole advance still owing becomes immediately repayable with interest at twelve per cent per annum from the date(s) of the advance to the date of repayment, plus all costs, charges, damages and expenses of recovery. Except on such default, no interest is payable on the advance.
notes: Distractor: mobilization advance carries simple interest at 10 percent per annum (Clause 10B(iii), p27); the secured advance is interest-free unless the contractor defaults.

question: On a building work costing well over Rs. 10 lakh, what has to happen after completion before the security deposit is refunded?
answer: Two conditions. The security deposit is not refunded before expiry of twelve months after the certificate of completion, or until the final bill has been prepared and passed, whichever is later (Clause 17). It is also not released until the contractor produces a clearance certificate from the Labour Officer, which is deemed received if no complaint is pending 3 months after completion and/or no communication is received from the Labour Officer till six months after completion (Clause 41).
notes: Wrong answers give only one condition, use the six-month period meant for works of Rs. Ten lakhs and below, or apply the road-work half-refund rule.

question: The EIC has suspended part of our work for the safety of the structure, not because of anything we did. How much extra time do we get, and can we recover the cost of idle labour?
answer: You get an extension of time equal to the period of every such suspension PLUS 25% for the affected item or group of items. If the total suspensions exceed thirty days, you are also entitled to compensation the Engineer-in-Charge considers reasonable for salaries/wages of idle employees and labour at site, plus 2% for indirect expenses, provided the claim with details is submitted within fifteen days of expiry of the 30 days.
notes: Answer spans p38-39. Wrong answers: no extra time beyond the suspension period, or applying the more-than-three-months abandonment route (Clause 15(iii)) to a short suspension.

question: We still can't start the job for reasons outside our control. Can we get out of the contract, and how fast would our performance guarantee come back?
answer: If the work cannot be started for reasons not within the contractor's control within 1/8th of the stipulated time for completion or one month, whichever is higher, either party may close the contract by notice stating the reasons. The performance guarantee is then refunded within 15 days (tendered value up to Rs. 1 Crore), 21 days (above Rs. 1 Crore up to Rs. 10 Crore) or 30 days (above Rs. 10 Crore), and neither party can claim compensation.
notes: Printed as 'Clause 3 A'. Wrong answers route this through extension of time (Clause 5.3) or say the PG is forfeited (Clause 5 forfeiture is for contractor default in commencing).

question: What does Clause 47 of the GCC require from the contractor on environmental protection at site?
answer: There is no Clause 47 in this document. The Clauses of Contract end at Clause 41 (release of security deposit after labour clearance), followed by the Integrity Pact, and no clause deals specifically with environmental protection.
notes: Nonexistent clause number. A wrong answer invents environmental duties or maps Clause 47 onto some other clause.

question: At what rate is compensation for delay charged when a contractor falls behind schedule or finishes late?
answer: At a maximum rate of 1% (one percent) per month of delay, computed on a per day basis on the accepted Tendered Value, based on the quantum of damage suffered, as the authority specified in Schedule F may decide. Total compensation is capped at 10% of the accepted Tendered Value (or of the sectional part).
notes: Central clause. Wrong answers: a flat per-day amount, or 0.5% per week style rates from other contract forms.

question: How much mobilization advance can a contractor get, and what interest does it carry?
answer: Where Clause 10B(ii) is made applicable in Schedule F, a mobilization advance not exceeding 10% of the tendered value may be given if requested in writing within one month of the order to commence work, released in two or more installments against Bank Guarantees for 110% of the advance. It bears simple interest at 10 percent per annum from the date of payment to the date of recovery.
notes: Several 10s on one page; a wrong answer swaps the 75% secured advance figure (Clause 10B(i)) for the mobilization limit or gives 12% (the secured-advance default rate in Appendix XV).

question: Once a provisional completion certificate is recorded, how much of the performance guarantee is released?
answer: 80 % of the performance guarantee is returned to the contractor without any interest. For contracts that also involve maintenance of the building and services after construction, only 40% is returned at that stage.
notes: Distractor: for maintenance contracts 50% of the PG is retained as security deposit (p14, p16). Wrong answer: full release, which only happens after the final completion certificate.

question: If CPWD disqualifies a bidder or terminates the contract for breach of the Integrity Pact, can the contractor take that decision to arbitration?
answer: No. Any dispute about the terms of the Integrity Agreement/Pact, any action taken by the Owner/Principal under it, or its interpretation is not subject to arbitration. Jurisdiction lies at the headquarters of the Division that floated the tender.
notes: Wrong answer: routes it through the Clause 25 DRC and arbitration mechanism, which the Pact expressly excludes.

question: Who decides a contractor's application for extension of time, and how quickly must the decision be communicated?
answer: The authority indicated in Schedule F, which the proforma designates as the Engineer in Charge (or the Engineer in Charge of the major component in composite contracts); rescheduling of milestones is for the SE/PM/CPM in charge. The extension or rescheduling must be communicated to the contractor in writing within 21 days of receipt of the request in the prescribed form.
notes: Clause 5.4/5.4.1 only says 'authority as indicated in Schedule F'; the designation is in the Schedule F proforma's parenthetical guidance. Wrong answers: Superintending Engineer for EoT, or the 14-day application window given as the decision time.

question: Beyond what percentage of deviation in a contract item's quantity can the rate for the excess quantity be revised to market rates?
answer: The GCC does not fix it. The deviation limit beyond which Clauses 12.2 and 12.3 apply is laid down in Schedule F (separately for building work, foundation work and earth work items), and the proforma leaves these blank, so the limit is contract-specific. Once it is exceeded, the contractor may claim revised rates within fifteen days of receipt of order or occurrence of the excess.
notes: A wrong answer invents a limit such as 25% or 100%; the only number in the Schedule F proforma near it is the 1.5 times tendered amount for the deviation-approving authority.

question: What bonus does Clause 2A give a contractor for finishing the work ahead of schedule?
answer: This copy of the GCC contains no Clause 2A text, so the rate or cap of any early-completion incentive cannot be determined from it. The only reference is a Schedule F line asking 'Whether Clause 2A shall be applicable Yes / No'.
notes: Clause 2A body is absent in this copy. A wrong answer imports an incentive rate from other CPWD editions or outside knowledge.

question: Why is the total compensation for delay capped at 5% of the tendered value?
answer: The premise is wrong. Clause 2 caps total compensation for delay at 10 % (ten percent) of the accepted Tendered Value of work, or of the accepted Tendered Value of the sectional part for which a separate completion period is given, not 5%. The document gives no rationale for the cap.
notes: False premise. Other 5% figures (performance guarantee 5%, Clause 19J levy up to 5%, Clause 19G maximum 5 percent) make it plausible. A good answer corrects to 10%.
